record.paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
record.original_question: In the free resolution of the Cauchy-Fueter module M_n from Theorem 3.2, prove or refute that every matrix in the resolution except P_2 has entries that are degree-one polynomials. The problem also asks for the analytic meaning of this observed linearity, since the authors report seeing it in computed examples but not knowing how to prove it in general.

evidence.quote: Problem: Prove that all the matrices which appear in Theorem 3.2 have entries which are degree one polynomials, with the exception of P_2.
However we have been unable to prove this fact in general, nor do we understand its analytical meaning.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the quaternions with basis $1,i,j,k$. For $n\geq 1$ and quaternionic variables $q_\ell = x_{\ell,0}+ix_{\ell,1}+jx_{\ell,2}+kx_{\ell,3}$, $\ell=1,\dots,n$, the Cauchy–Fueter operator in the $\ell$-th variable is
$$\partial_{\bar q_\ell} = \partial_{x_{\ell,0}} + i\,\partial_{x_{\ell,1}} + j\,\partial_{x_{\ell,2}} + k\,\partial_{x_{\ell,3}}.$$
After identifying $\mathbb{H}\cong\mathbb{C}^2$, the operator $\partial_{\bar q_\ell}$ corresponds to a $2\times 2$ matrix of first-order constant-coefficient differential operators with polynomial symbol $P_\ell\in \operatorname{Mat}_{2\times 2}(R)$, where $R = \mathbb{C}[z_{\ell,\alpha}\colon \ell=1,\dots,n,\ \alpha=1,2,3,4]$ is a polynomial ring with $4n$ indeterminates corresponding to the Fourier symbols of the $4n$ real partial derivatives.

Let $P\in \operatorname{Mat}_{2n\times 2}(R)$ be the column matrix obtained by stacking $P_1,\dots,P_n$, and let $M_n = \operatorname{coker}(P^T\colon R^{2n}\to R^{2})^{\vee}$ be the associated Cauchy–Fueter module (viewed as the $R$-module whose minimal free resolution computes the syzygies of $P$). There exists a minimal graded free resolution
$$0\to R^{b_N}\xrightarrow{P_N}\cdots\xrightarrow{P_3} R^{b_2}\xrightarrow{P_2} R^{b_1}\xrightarrow{P_1} R^{b_0}\to M_n\to 0.$$

Prove or disprove: for every $n\geq 2$ and every $i\in\{1,3,4,\dots,N\}$ (that is, for every matrix in the resolution other than $P_2$), all nonzero entries of the matrix $P_i$ are homogeneous polynomials of degree exactly one in $R$.

In addition, provide an analytic interpretation of this linearity in terms of the Cauchy–Fueter complex.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any paper that explicitly proves or disproves the linearity of all matrices (other than the second) in the minimal free resolution of the Cauchy–Fueter module $M_n$, nor any work giving an analytic interpretation of this phenomenon. The status appears unverified from publicly available sources.

status_evidence.title: The Cauchy-Fueter System and Its Variations
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Cauchy–Fueter systems in several quaternionic variables and their associated complexes/resolutions.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys of the Cauchy–Fueter system describe its resolutions but do not record a proof of the conjectured linearity of all matrices other than P_2.

status_evidence.title: Cauchy-Riemann operators and local slice analysis over real alternative algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Related work on Cauchy–Riemann/Cauchy–Fueter operators in hypercomplex analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature on Cauchy–Fueter operators does not appear to contain a resolution of the linearity question.
